narrative:
On August 11, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 41.2%, taking up 1,066 matters out of 2,589 scheduled cases across 48 judges. This operational efficiency reflects a slight rebound from the 39.6% hearing rate logged on August 7 (936 of 2,363 cases heard), though it remains beneath the 45.6% rate achieved on August 6 (1,167 of 2,560 cases heard).

Judicial output varied across court halls. Workload clearance was led by Justice M. Nagaprasanna in Hall 14, who heard 131 total matters across multiple cause lists, including 85 out of 141 cases on the main list (60.3%). In Hall 19, Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty handled the largest single-judge docket, hearing 102 of 268 scheduled matters (38.1%). High conversion rates were also logged in Hall 4 by the bench of Justices D.K. Singh and H. Shanthi Bhushan, hearing 33 of 44 cases (75.0%). Conversely, lists in Halls 34 and 35 registered no heard matters.

Stage-wise conversion highlights procedural bottlenecking in substantive hearings. Matters listed under Orders accounted for the highest volume and converted well, with 384 of 791 heard (48.5%). In contrast, Final Hearing matters experienced lower throughput, with only 133 of 636 scheduled cases reaching a hearing (20.9%). 

Across case types, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the bulk of court listings, achieving a 40.6% hearing rate (409 of 1,007 heard). Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) achieved the highest resolution rate among major case categories at 50.3% (161 of 320 heard), while Regular First Appeals (RFA) lagged significantly with a 23.7% hearing rate (53 of 224 heard).
